purpose: Define evidence dimensions for comparing terrestrial environments with Mars surface mission contexts. This file defines requirements and current availability; it is not a scoring model.
scientificCautions: Terrestrial gravity, atmospheric pressure and composition, radiation environment, and planetary history differ from Mars.
NASA POWER solar radiation is not ultraviolet radiation.
A point DEM elevation sample does not characterize slope, roughness, obstacles, or regional terrain diversity.
GLiM is generalized surface lithology mapping, not site-level field verification or mineral detection.
Lithology does not establish mineral identity or concentration.
Five original atlas points and three supplementary point-area records have retrievals; coordinates are approximate or represent site areas, and point queries may not represent the named feature.
No similarity score, mission score, ranking, or scientific confidence score is defined.

dimensions.name: Climate and thermal environment
dimensions.whyItMatters: Thermal conditions and day-to-day variability affect surface operations, materials, and analog interpretation.

factors.name: Daily mean air temperature
factors.definition: NASA POWER T2M daily gridded air temperature at 2 m.

evidenceAvailability.dataset: Daily Point API; meteorological sources reported by response
evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Gridded point product; source support is variable/source dependent, not a site observation
evidenceAvailability.processingMethod: Normalized daily value; NASA missing sentinel represented as null

limitations: Subset: five original atlas sites plus three supplementary point-area sites; the remaining 23 references have no matching retrieved record.
Gridded estimate and approximate atlas coordinates limit site-specific interpretation.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Document parameter-specific source support and retrieve a scientifically justified broader sample.

factors.name: Daily maximum and minimum air temperature
factors.definition: NASA POWER T2M_MAX and T2M_MIN at 2 m; retain each parameter distinctly.

evidenceAvailability.dataset: Daily Point API; meteorological sources reported by response
evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Gridded point product; source support is variable/source dependent

limitations: Not in situ site measurements; five original atlas sites plus three supplementary point-area records have retrievals; coverage is not complete.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Expand coverage and validate product/source provenance per parameter.

factors.name: Daily temperature range
factors.definition: Derived daily T2M_MAX minus T2M_MIN when both source values are present.

evidenceAvailability.processingMethod: T2M_MAX - T2M_MIN; null if either input is missing

limitations: Derived from gridded values; no independent measurement.

factors.name: Relative humidity
factors.definition: NASA POWER RH2M relative humidity at 2 m.

evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Gridded point product; source support is variable/source dependent

limitations: Relative humidity is not a direct measure of water availability or soil moisture.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Pair with independently sourced surface/soil moisture or water-balance evidence if required.

factors.name: Precipitation
factors.definition: NASA POWER PRECTOTCORR corrected daily precipitation; annual totals require complete daily coverage under the existing pipeline rule.
factors.unit: mm/day; annual total mm/year only for complete calendar years

evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Gridded point product; source support is variable/source dependent
evidenceAvailability.temporalResolution: Daily; complete-year annual aggregation where available
evidenceAvailability.processingMethod: Valid daily values summed by calendar year; incomplete annual sum is not labeled complete

limitations: Precipitation alone is not an aridity index or a complete hydrological characterization.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Research a defensible evapotranspiration/water-balance source and method before claiming aridity.

factors.name: Wind speed
factors.definition: NASA POWER WS10M daily wind speed at 10 m.

evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Gridded point product; source support is variable/source dependent

limitations: Does not characterize gusts, dust lifting, or local sheltering.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Assess dust and gust observations separately if mission requirements justify them.

factors.name: Surface shortwave radiation
factors.definition: NASA POWER ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN all-sky surface shortwave downward radiation.

evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Gridded point product; source support is variable/source dependent

limitations: This broadband solar radiation measure is not UV irradiance, UV index, or radiation dose.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Select a validated UV/ionizing-radiation dataset separately if needed; do not substitute this field.

factors.name: Aridity or climatic water balance
factors.definition: A documented index requiring precipitation and a defensible potential evapotranspiration or water-balance method.
factors.unit: Index and method to be selected and documented
limitations: Precipitation alone cannot establish aridity.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Select a validated evapotranspiration source and pre-register index definition.

dimensions.name: Atmospheric and environmental context
dimensions.whyItMatters: Atmospheric pressure, composition, dust, and radiation influence environmental similarity and operations, but terrestrial conditions cannot reproduce Mars atmospheric conditions.

factors.name: Surface pressure
factors.definition: Measured terrestrial atmospheric pressure with documented sensor/product, height, and temporal support.
limitations: No surface pressure was retrieved in M02; do not assume it is present in NASA POWER output.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Evaluate an authoritative source and verify parameter metadata before integration.

factors.name: Ultraviolet radiation
factors.definition: Direct UV irradiance or dose with spectral band and exposure interval explicitly defined.
factors.unit: Band-specific W/m² or dose unit to be selected
limitations: NASA POWER shortwave radiation is not UV.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Identify a validated UV source; do not infer from broadband solar radiation.

factors.name: Dust and aerosol environment
factors.definition: Direct aerosol/dust observation or documented satellite-derived proxy with method and uncertainty.
limitations: Wind speed alone does not establish dust loading or lifting.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Review aerosol products and validation over arid sites.

dimensions.name: Terrain and topography
dimensions.whyItMatters: Surface geometry affects mobility, landing and instrument deployment, but terrain characterization requires spatial neighborhoods and more than a single elevation sample.

factors.name: Point surface elevation
factors.definition: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 DSM pixel elevation sampled at the atlas coordinate.
factors.unit: m relative to EGM2008 vertical datum

evidenceAvailability.provider: Copernicus DEM via AWS Public Dataset
evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Nominal 1 arc-second (~30 m); actual pixel spacing varies with latitude
evidenceAvailability.processingMethod: Single raster pixel sampled at requested atlas coordinate; DSM value, not bare-earth guarantee

limitations: Approximate atlas coordinates may not identify the named feature.
One point does not describe site relief, slope, roughness, obstacles, or terrain diversity.
DSM may include surface objects.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Extract validated neighborhoods/terrain derivatives from a documented DEM workflow when mission needs are specified.

factors.name: Slope, roughness, and local relief
factors.definition: Neighborhood terrain metrics with declared window size, algorithm, resolution, and NoData treatment.
factors.unit: Slope degrees; roughness and relief require explicitly defined units/metric
limitations: M03 retrieves point elevation only; it does not calculate terrain derivatives.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Define neighborhood scale and reproducible algorithms before extraction.

dimensions.name: Geological and lithological context
dimensions.whyItMatters: Mapped rock classes and formation processes can guide analog selection, but scale, mapping generalization, and local evidence quality must be explicit.

factors.name: Mapped lithology
factors.definition: Original GLiM v1.1 classification levels and descriptions returned for polygons intersecting the requested point; preserve source hierarchy.
factors.unit: Source categorical codes/descriptions (levels xx, yy, zz kept separate)

evidenceAvailability.dataset: GLiM Niveau I service layer; original returned attributes preserved
evidenceAvailability.observationPeriod: Published map/database version; not a time series
evidenceAvailability.spatialResolution: Global generalized map; approximately 1:3.75 million map scale documented by GLiM source
evidenceAvailability.processingMethod: Point-in-polygon service query; all intersecting features retained

limitations: Approximate coordinates and generalized polygon scale make this area-level mapped evidence, not field truth.
Codes such as No Data or Water Bodies must remain source classifications.
Lithology is not mineral detection.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Acquire site-specific geological mapping or field-verified samples for selected locations.

factors.name: Mineral evidence
factors.definition: Location-specific mineral observations with method, source, and verification status; never inferred solely from lithology.
factors.unit: Mineral identity and method-specific concentration/unit if measured
limitations: GLiM does not provide precise mineralogy; some atlas mineral descriptions are inferred or weakly supported.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Collect site-specific assay, spectroscopy, or peer-reviewed field observations with traceable location.

factors.name: Geological formation and process descriptions
factors.definition: Traceable site or regional geological observations and process interpretations, with evidence quality distinguished from narrative context.
factors.unit: Qualitative evidence with source and quality metadata

evidenceAvailability.processingMethod: Legacy descriptive text preserved; not newly verified by M05

limitations: Descriptions vary in detail and require independent verification.
Research document is context, not a numerical observation dataset.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Review each claim against primary geological references and identify location-specific evidence.

dimensions.name: Surface materials, sediments, and hydrological context
dimensions.whyItMatters: Material properties and water-related processes influence rover mobility, sampling, drilling, and environmental interpretation, but mapped classes are not local quantitative measurements.

factors.name: Mapped surface lithology/material class
factors.definition: Only source-classified GLiM surface lithology; no conversion to mineral composition or quantitative surface fractions.
factors.unit: Original GLiM category codes and descriptions

evidenceAvailability.processingMethod: Original polygon attributes preserved without mineral inference

limitations: Does not quantify sand/rock fraction, grain size, regolith depth, or local obstacles.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Identify validated high-resolution land-surface/material observations for operational sites.

factors.name: Sediment and regolith properties
factors.definition: Measured grain size, sediment depth, bearing properties, or subsurface regolith profile with sampling method.
limitations: No quantitative site-linked material measurements are present in M01–M04.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Source field measurements or mission-relevant validated remote sensing with explicit uncertainty.

factors.name: Surface and subsurface hydrological context
factors.definition: Direct evidence for surface water, groundwater, ice, salts, drainage, or seasonal hydrological processes.
limitations: Precipitation alone does not establish persistent water, groundwater, ice, or salt distribution.
factors.nextEvidenceNeed: Define mission-relevant hydrological observations and evaluate authoritative datasets.

missions.name: Rover surface testing
missions.objective: Describe surface mobility and operational terrain evidence without inferring suitability from a point elevation.
limitations: Slope, roughness, local relief, quantitative material properties, and obstacles are not currently available.
nonGoals: No rover suitability score or ranking.
No inference of obstacle safety from elevation or GLiM.

missions.name: Geological surface exploration
missions.objective: Organize mapped lithology and traceable geological/mineral evidence while preserving evidence quality.
limitations: GLiM mapped lithology is available for five original atlas points and three supplementary point-area records but is generalized; location-specific mineral verification is unavailable.

missions.name: Extreme environment operations
missions.objective: Describe measured thermal and meteorological stressors with explicit temporal coverage and product provenance.
limitations: NASA POWER daily histories exist for five original atlas sites and three supplementary point-area records; aridity, UV, dust, and directly retrieved surface pressure are unavailable. Earth atmospheric conditions differ fundamentally from Mars.
nonGoals: Solar radiation is not UV or radiation dose.

missions.name: Drilling and subsurface exploration
missions.objective: Identify direct subsurface evidence relevant to drilling and sampling; surface proxies alone are inadequate.
limitations: No sediment thickness, buried structures, GPR, subsurface profile, or geotechnical measurements are available.
nonGoals: No drilling suitability score from surface climate, elevation, or generalized lithology.
